Drop rows that match a condition

Source: R/filter.R
filter_out.tbl_gpu.Rd

The complement of filter.tbl_gpu(), like dplyr::filter_out(): all conditions are combined with AND first, then the rows where that combination is TRUE are dropped. Rows where it is FALSE or NA are kept (so this is not filter(!cond)). With no conditions every row is dropped. It runs like filter(): the same conditions run on the GPU, with the same window predicates, .by, CPU fallbacks, and eager and lazy modes.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'tbl_gpu'
filter_out(.data, ..., .by = NULL, .preserve = FALSE)

Arguments

.data

A tbl_gpu object created by tbl_gpu().

...

Logical expressions; rows where all of them are TRUE are dropped.

.by

Optional grouping columns for this call only (tidyselect), run on the GPU: filter(df, x > mean(x), .by = g) gives the same rows as df |> group_by(g) |> filter(x > mean(x)) |> ungroup(), and the result is ungrouped. Supplying .by when .data is already grouped (via group_by()) is an error, as in dplyr.

.preserve

Whether to keep the groups the filter emptied. With TRUE, a group_by()-grouped result keeps the input's group keys (empty groups included) for group_data(), collect() and summarise(), like dplyr (see group_by.tbl_gpu() for what carries them on). FALSE recomputes the groups from the remaining rows.

Value

A tbl_gpu object without the rows where all conditions are TRUE.
